background: Banco Santander is Spain's largest bank and one of the largest in the eurozone, run as a group of self-funded national subsidiaries across Spain, the UK, Brazil, Mexico, the US and elsewhere, with retail and commercial banking at its core.
synthesis: Ratings are A+ on average across all three main agencies and none is lower, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of them on 12 May 2026. Capital is the weak point, with CET1 of 14.0% in the bottom quarter of peers and leverage of 4.8% below the median; liquidity is mixed, LCR of 147% below the median against NSFR of 124% above it. CET1 has risen 1.0 points since 30 Jun 2025 while the other three ratios are broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The newest flagged item, on 23 Sep 2026, is a board change at the Chilean subsidiary, alongside older items on that unit's results and a record group profit.
